source_act: Section 138, Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881
user_query: A business client gave me a cheque of Rs 4 lakhs that bounced due to 'Insufficient Funds'. What is the exact procedure to take legal action?
legal_text_raw: You must send a formal Statutory Legal Demand Notice in writing within 30 days of receiving the cheque bounce memo from the bank, giving the drawer 15 days to pay. If they fail to pay within 15 days, you must file a criminal complaint under Section 138 NI Act before the Magistrate within 30 days.

If they fail to pay within 15 days, you must file a criminal complaint under Section 138 NI Act before the Magistrate within 30 days.

source_act: Section 102, Code of Criminal Procedure / Section 106 BNSS & Banking Regulations
user_query: Can a bank freeze my savings account without any court order or police notice?
legal_text_raw: A bank cannot arbitrarily freeze an account on its own whim. Account freezes are only legally permissible pursuant to a formal order from a Magistrate, a statutory tax authority (IT/GST), an order under Section 106 BNSS by police during investigation, or failure to comply with mandatory KYC after proper notice.

source_act: Civil Procedure Code & Sarfaesi Act / Consumer Jurisprudence
user_query: Can I be arrested or sent to jail immediately if my loan EMI or credit card bill defaults?
legal_text_raw: No. Loan or credit card default is purely a civil dispute, not a criminal offense. Banks cannot get you arrested for simply being unable to pay an unsecured loan. They can only initiate civil recovery suits or debt recovery tribunal proceedings. Arrest is only possible in deliberate fraud or dishonored cheques.

source_act: Section 13(2) & 13(4), SARFAESI Act, 2002

legal_text_raw: No. The bank must first issue a mandatory 60-day notice under Section 13(2) specifying the amount due. The borrower has the statutory right to raise objections, which the bank must answer within 15 days. Only after 60 days can the bank issue a possession notice under Section 13(4), appealable before the DRT.

source_act: ICICI Bank v. Prakash Kaur (Supreme Court of India, 2007)
user_query: Can a private financier confiscate my car on the road through musclemen if I miss two car loan EMIs?

Repossession must follow due legal process with prior written notice, inventory recording, and opportunity to clear arrears. Forcible seizure constitutes criminal theft and robbery.

legal_text_raw: Yes. The Supreme Court held that Section 138 applies to cheques issued for discharge 'in whole or in part of any debt or other liability'. A cheque issued by a guarantor to discharge the principal borrower's debt falls squarely within Section 138.

source_act: Section 141, Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881
user_query: Can a company director be held liable for a cheque bounce if they resigned before the cheque was issued?
legal_text_raw: No. A director who formally resigned and whose resignation was notified to the Registrar of Companies (Form DIR-12) before the cheque was issued or presented cannot be prosecuted under Section 141, as they were not in charge of company affairs at the time.
layman_explanation: No. A director who formally resigned and whose resignation was notified to the Registrar of Companies (Form DIR-12) before the cheque was issued or presented cannot be prosecuted under Section 141, as they were not in charge of company affairs at the time.
